The key component for being an employee vs a contractor is whether a company dictates /When/ a worker does a job. For example, a traditional taxi company is an employer because they dictate that workers will work certain shifts. Uber drivers are absolutely not employees because exactly like contractors they can choose whether or not to accept a ride and when they choose to work.

Uber setting prices has absolutely nothing to do with whether workers are employees or contractors, anymore than Bob's Grain Silo offering to pay $7/bushel for corn makes them an employer of every farmer in the area. Bob's grain silo is simply offering a price to contractors on a take-it-or-leave it basis, the same as Uber does.

Which is honestly pretty similar to Ebay - buying and selling homogenous, high volume items on Ebay tends to arrive at a de-facto take-it-or-leave it price pretty quickly (market equilibrium). Uber just uses software algorithms to help riders and drivers determine this market equilibrium price programatically based on supply and demand.
